content: Polygonum aviculare, also known as Common Knotgrass, is a plant that belongs to the same family as buckwheat and dock. It is also referred to by other names, such as birdweed, pigweed, and lowgrass. This plant is an annual species that typically grows in fields and wastelands. It produces small white flowers that bloom from June to October. In folklore, Nicholas Culpeper, a 17th-century herbalist, noted that this plant is astrologically governed by Saturn and the zodiac sign Capricorn. From a herbalism perspective, Culpeper recommended the use of knotweed to treat conditions involving the spitting of blood. In modern herbal medicine, it is used to address a variety of conditions, including dysentery, excessive menstrual bleeding, lung disorders, bronchitis, jaundice, and the presence of gallstones or kidney stones. However, it is important to note that not all of these applications are supported by scientific evidence. Pharmacologically, the plant exhibits properties such as being an astringent, a coagulant, a diuretic, and an expectorant. There are several subspecies of Polygonum aviculare, including: Polygonum aviculare subsp. aviculare Polygonum aviculare subsp. depressum (Meisn.) Arcang.
